country_data.price_source: Botswana Agricultural Marketing Board scheduled-produce producer/market price schedule, July/August 2026, reproduced by The Farmers' Platform. Range: Tswana cowpeas Grade 2 BWP 7.70/kg to Black-eye cowpeas Grade 1 BWP 13.50/kg; intermediate observations include Tswana Grade 1 BWP 11.00/kg and Black-eye Grade 2 BWP 9.45/kg.
country_data.source: Botswana-specific BAMB cowpea producer/market price schedule (July/August 2026); yield and production cost remain Africa benchmark estimates, not Botswana farm measurements or enterprise budgets.
country_data.cost_source: Africa benchmark estimate; not a Botswana-specific farmer-paid input or enterprise budget. Botswana 2026/27 Lemang Dijo voucher values are recorded separately as subsidy evidence only.
country_data.yield_source: Botswana-specific evidence: national cowpea yield reported around 139 kg/ha by Statistics Botswana (2013); peer-reviewed Botswana field-evaluation paper reports national average around 300 kg/ha and trial genotype yields ranging 318–866 kg/ha. The high scenario is an observed trial-genotype ceiling, not a national commercial average.
country_data.seed_rate_source: Seed Co Botswana rain-fed crop guidance: cowpeas 10 kg/ha. This is a recommended sowing rate, not a seed price.
country_data.cost_reference: Botswana's 2026/27 Lemang Dijo one-hectare voucher lists programme support values for seeds (P580), harrowing (P495), ploughing (P1,045), planting (P495), pesticides/herbicides (P480), and fertiliser support up to P3,600 after soil testing. These are subsidy/voucher values, not a complete farmer-paid cowpea enterprise budget; they are not substituted for the calculator's disclosed benchmark cost.
country_data.local_market_demand_reference: Botswana Agricultural Marketing Board states demand for Tswana cowpeas currently exceeds supply and that it promotes production; BAMB buys Tswana and Black-eyed cowpeas from local farmers.
country_data.local_production_suitability_reference: BAMB describes Tswana cowpeas as drought tolerant and suitable for cultivation throughout Botswana; Black-eyed cowpeas can be produced successfully in most areas.
country_data.local_market_and_suitability_source: Botswana Agricultural Marketing Board, Pulses/Beans information page
country_data.local_market_and_suitability_note: Official market and agronomic context only. The BAMB statement confirms local procurement and a reported supply gap but does not quantify demand, guarantee a purchase, or establish a farm budget. The existing cowpea selling-price and yield inputs remain supported by their separately cited sources; the production cost remains an Africa benchmark proxy.
